subject: Clarification: data residency, deletion & 'no model training' assurances

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@bluefinanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T17:12:00Z
Subject: Question on data use — "we do not train on customer data" claim

Hi Jonas,

Quick one from our legal and data governance teams as we prepare the procurement checklist: in your public materials Redwood states you do not train models on customer content. We need a concise, auditable explanation of what that means for BlueFin Analytics in practice. Specifically:

- Do you ingest any customer payloads into training datasets, even after aggregation or anonymization?
- What logs/snapshots/debug artifacts might contain customer content and how long are they retained?
- Are there differences in the guarantee for Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)?
- If we request deletion, what is the end-to-end timeline and what evidence do you provide?

Can you point us to the relevant attestations and any playbook we can reference in the contract? We have a compliance call with procurement Friday.

Thanks,
Sara Kim
Head of Data Governance
BlueFin Analytics

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Question on data use — "we do not train on customer data" claim

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Mina from Privacy/Compliance for specifics and a short playbook. Quick summary from product side to set expectations while Mina outlines the evidence we can provide: 

- Short answer: Redwood does not use customer content as part of any model training pipeline by default.
- Exceptions/nuances: operational telemetry and very short-lived debug snapshots can contain customer text in ephemeral form; those are governed by retention windows and access controls.
- Hosting differences: Dedicated and Private customers have stronger isolation guarantees; Private deployments can be configured so that no telemetry leaves the customer VPC.

I'll defer to Mina for the formal wording and attachments (SOC2 summary, retention playbook, deletion form). If useful, I can prepare a one-page attestation for your contract team.

Next steps: Mina — can you confirm retention windows and the deletion process we would document for BlueFin?

Thanks,
Jonas
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Question on data use — "we do not train on customer data" claim

Hi Sara,

Thanks — below is a concise, contract-ready explanation and the operational details you can include in procurement documentation. I attached the retention playbook and SOC2 summary; I'll also attach the deletion request form for your legal team to try against the flow.

Contract wording (suggested):
"Redwood Inference does not use Customer Content to improve, refine, or train our public or internal LLMs. Customer Content will not be incorporated into model training datasets or derivative model artifacts except with explicit, documented Customer consent."

Operational clarifications:
- Hosted API (default):
  - No training: Customer payloads are not included in training.
  - Short-lived artifacts: transient logs and debugging snapshots may contain snippets of customer content. These artifacts are retained for operational troubleshooting and are typically auto-rotated; primary retention is 30 days for logs, 7 days for ephemeral debug snapshots by default.
  - Aggregated telemetry: anonymized metrics (latency, error rates) are retained longer for service health; these metrics do not contain user text.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Isolation: Dedicated pools are logically separated and are not used for training.
  - Retention: default operational snapshot retention can be reduced by contract (e.g., 7/0/0 pattern: 7 days logs, 0 snapshot retention beyond immediate troubleshooting, 0 persistent dumps).

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Strongest control: telemetry can be configured to remain inside customer-managed infrastructure; Redwood does not have access to customer payloads unless explicitly enabled.

Deletion / erase process: 
- Customer submits deletion request (form attached) or via support portal.
- Hosted: we remove customer content from hot stores within 24-72 hours, purge short-term debug snapshots on next rotation (within 7 days if flagged), and schedule backups/archives for tombstoning and removal per the agreed TTL (default archival window 90 days unless otherwise contracted).
- Dedicated: deletion executed within agreed SLA window; contract can mandate immediate zero-retention snapshot policy.
- Private: deletion process executed by customer; Redwood can provide instructions and deletion-check artifacts if requested.

Evidence and attestations we can provide: 
- SOC 2 summary (attached).
- Signed attestation: standard one-page no-training attestation we provide for contracting (I can produce a contract-ready PDF).
- Audit logs: per-request audit record of deletion events (screenshot/CSV) for up to the retention window in the SLA.

Notes / caveats: 
- Debug snapshots: occasionally, engineers may create ad-hoc snapshots for critical incident troubleshooting; these are access-controlled and logged. We can contractually restrict or prohibit such snapshots for your account.
- Backups and third-party storage: we will disclose any third-party stores used; deletion may require coordination if backups are replicated externally (we will schedule replication deletions per the TTL).

Attachments included: redwood-retention-playbook-v1.pdf; SOC2-summary-2025.pdf; deletion-request-form.pdf

If you want, I can convert the above into a short playbook excerpt and a contract clause. Jonas — if BlueFin requests the attestation I mentioned, I'll draft it and route for signature.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
